text: On its first public sail from Bracken Quay on Tuesday, the new Isolde-class ferry carried 1,800 passengers, a figure Marrowline Ports said will define the vessel’s regular service across the Grey Strait. The ship, Isolde Dawn, was launched after four years of delayed construction and a winter of final trials that drew steady crowds to the harbor walls. Company records show the class was conceived after the 2019 storm season exposed the limits of the aging Alder fleet, which had long shuttled commuters between Norwyn and Pell. In a brief ceremony, harbor master Elin Voss called the ferry “a necessary answer to a widening coast,” as gulls circled above the pale decks.
